errors.why: Here གྲངས་ཅན means an enumeration (the 'and so forth' sets out the list colour etc.), not the Sāṃkhya school.

note: A terse lemma-by-lemma commentary rendered reasonably; one misidentified term.

errors.english: Dependence is definitely not possible in that way.
errors.why: With the preceding མི་ the sentence says that what does NOT depend on their benefit cannot be restricted to that place/time; the English makes dependence impossible.

errors.english: If the head of Indra [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is the standard Pramāṇavārttika example of an anthill, whose vapour looks like smoke; the note is wrong.

fix.find: If the head of Indra [note: a reference to a specific type of grass or a mythological origin point]
fix.replace: If an anthill (śakramūrdhan, lit. "Indra's head") [note: an anthill, whose vapour resembles smoke]

errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung (gomaya), the stock example of a dissimilar source from which plants are seen to arise.

note: The causal argument is followed, but the anthill and cow-dung examples, central to the passage, are mistranslated.

errors.english: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
errors.why: Recognition and the parts produce the cognition OF the whole; the whole is the object, not the producer.

fix.find: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
fix.replace: The text states that [recognition and the parts] produce the cognition of the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin), the whole composed of parts.

errors.english: because there is no third cognition other than recognition and memory, the objection is raised by the phrase "but if" and so forth.
errors.why: Two separate glosses: 'from that' is explained by there being no third cognition; separately, 'but if' etc. introduces an objection.

errors.english: then the valid means of knowledge would be consistent with the object
errors.why: The point is that the word 'pramāṇa' would then be meaningful/purposeful, not that cognition accords with its object.

note: Argument about the avayavin is broadly tracked, but case roles and the segmentation of glosses slip in places.

errors.english: Physical effort while remaining on land included within the boundary, such as by throwing a weapon;
errors.why: Standing on land within the boundary qualifies the monk for all three modes (body, speech, mind), not only the physical one.
Means the toll obligation has not been incurred/levied, not 'without attachment'.

errors.english: If the carrier is positioned on land belonging to the boundary but has no specific purpose, there is no downfall.
errors.why: No offence where [the mantra/medicine power] needs no carrier standing within the boundary; it is not about the carrier lacking a purpose.

note: Vinaya toll-evasion casuistry is roughly conveyed but several conditions are misparsed.

errors.english: the howling lords of those who commit unwholesome deeds inflict suffering
errors.why: It is the evil-doers themselves who cry out piteously in their suffering, not 'lords' inflicting suffering.

note: Sound rendering of the cetanā/cetayitvā karma division and the 'supreme sage' gloss.

errors.english: "externalists" [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
errors.why: The commentary itself glosses ཕྱི་རོལ་པ as what is external to the universal, i.e. the particulars, not a philosophical school.
